scenes.heading: Limitations of Batch Processing
scenes.narration: For all its strengths, batch processing has real limitations that make it the wrong choice for some workloads.

scenes.heading: Key limitations
bullets: Latency, since results wait for the next run
No real-time visibility into fresh data
Errors surface late, at the next batch
scenes.narration: The biggest limitation of batch processing is latency, because results only appear after the next scheduled run. This means there is no real-time visibility into data as it arrives. Errors also surface late, often only discovered when the following batch runs. As a result, batch is a poor fit for decisions that must be made in the moment.

scenes.heading: When batch falls short
scenes.narration: Batch struggles with fraud detection, live monitoring, and instant personalization because all of these need answers immediately. Streaming handles these cases by processing events the moment they occur. When timeliness is critical, streaming or hybrid approaches are the better choice.

scenes.text: Batch processing's latency makes it unsuitable for real-time needs; reach for streaming when timing is critical.
scenes.narration: The key takeaway is that batch processing's inherent latency makes it unsuitable for real-time needs, so reach for streaming whenever timing is critical.
